responses: Kardan University was established in 2002 in Kabul by its founder Roeen Rahmani, making it the very first private university in Afghanistan. Kardan University was founded in 2002 by Roeen Rahmani, at a time when Afghanistan was opening to new opportunities in education. It began with only 15 students in a single classroom, offering short courses in business and management. The name “Kardan” means competence in Dari, reflecting its mission to build capable professionals. Within just a few years, the institute grew rapidly, and in 2006 it was officially recognized as a university by the Ministry of Higher Education. From those modest beginnings, Kardan expanded into multiple campuses in Kabul, offering undergraduate and graduate programs in business, IT, engineering, and social sciences. It became the first private university in Afghanistan, setting a model for others to follow. Over time, Kardan earned international accreditations, joined global networks, and launched research journals and policy forums. Today, it is known for producing thousands of graduates who contribute to Afghanistan’s development, while still carrying the spirit of its humble start.

Kardan University started its journey in 2002, during a time when Afghanistan was opening to private education. Its founder, Roeen Rahmani, began with a single classroom and a vision to transform learning. From those modest beginnings, Kardan grew rapidly, gaining recognition from the Ministry of Higher Education in 2006 and later achieving international accreditation. It has pioneered online education during the COVID-19 pandemic, launched graduate programs, and built a reputation as a center for excellence. Today, it stands as a symbol of progress, with thousands of students and alumni shaping Afghanistan’s future.

The journey of Kardan University began in 2002, when its founder Roeen Rahmani opened a small classroom with just 15 students. At that time, private higher education was unheard of in Afghanistan, so Kardan’s establishment was groundbreaking. By 2006, the Ministry of Higher Education granted it full university status, making it the first licensed private university in the country. Over the years, Kardan grew steadily, adding new faculties, programs, and campuses. It introduced graduate degrees, built strong international partnerships, and became the first Afghan university to join the Global Business School Network. Kardan also gained accreditation from organizations like ACBSP and IACBE, ensuring its programs met international standards. Today, it has educated more than 30,000 graduates, and is recognized as a leader in innovation, research, and quality education in Afghanistan. Its history is a story of vision, resilience, and growth from a single classroom to a respected institution.

The story of Kardan University is one of resilience and vision. Founded in 2002, it was Afghanistan’s first privately owned higher education institution, created to provide quality education during a period of national rebuilding. Starting with a handful of students, it quickly expanded and became a full university in 2006. Over the years, Kardan has achieved national and international accreditations (including ACBSP and IACBE) and has produced more than 30,000 graduates. Its journey reflects the broader transformation of Afghan education, from modest beginnings to global recognition.

responses: To register for any graduate program at Kardan University, you must meet a minimum CGPA of 2.0 or 65% in your undergraduate degree. You also need to pass the pre-admission entry test and successfully complete an interview conducted after the test. An intermediate level of English proficiency is required, and you must submit all necessary documents – including an attested bachelor's degree from a MoHE-recognized institution, attested high school certificate, Tazkira, four passport photos, and an updated CV. This comprehensive evaluation ensures we admit only the most qualified and motivated students. 🎓📋

Undergraduate registration requirements are straightforward but essential. You must pass the pre-admission entry test, submit a Ministry of Education attested 12th grade certificate and transcript, provide a copy of your National Identity Card (Tazkira), and bring four recent passport-size photographs. Meeting these criteria confirms your academic readiness and eligibility for our bachelor's programs. We encourage you to prepare these documents well in advance to avoid any delays in your registration. 📸🆔

For graduate applicants, the entry test and interview are critical components of your registration. After successfully passing the test, you'll be invited for an interview where we assess your motivation, communication skills, and suitability for the program. English proficiency at an intermediate level is also non-negotiable – you'll need to demonstrate your ability to understand and participate in academic discussions. If you're unsure about your English level, consider taking a practice test or enrolling in a preparatory course. 🧠🗣️

Here is a complete checklist of documents required for graduate registration:
  • Attested bachelor's degree from a MoHE-recognized higher education institution.
  • High school certificate attested by the Ministry of Education.
  • Copy of your National Identity Card (Tazkira).
  • Four recent passport-size photographs.
  • An updated Curriculum Vitae (CV) highlighting your academic and professional achievements.
Ensure all attestations are done before you visit the campus – missing or incorrect documents can delay your registration. 📂✅

For undergraduate applicants, the document checklist is simpler but equally important:
  • Ministry of Education attested 12th grade certificate and transcript.
  • Copy of your National Identity Card (Tazkira).
  • Four recent passport-size photographs.
  • Successful completion of the pre-admission entry test.
These documents verify your educational background and identity. Make sure your 12th grade certificate is properly attested – this is a mandatory requirement set by the Ministry of Higher Education. 📑🆔

The pre-admission entry test is mandatory for all levels – both undergraduate and graduate. It assesses your general knowledge, analytical skills, and aptitude for the program you're applying to. For graduate applicants, the interview that follows the test is equally important – it's your chance to showcase your passion, clarity of goals, and readiness for advanced study. We recommend preparing thoroughly for both stages by reviewing sample questions and practicing your communication skills. 📝🎯

Attestation is a crucial step in the registration process. For graduate applicants, your bachelor's degree must be attested by the Ministry of Higher Education. For undergraduate applicants, your 12th grade certificate must be attested by the Ministry of Education. These attestations confirm the authenticity of your academic credentials. Plan ahead – attestation can take time, and we cannot process incomplete applications. We suggest starting this process at least a few weeks before you intend to submit your registration. 🏛️⏳

Meeting the CGPA requirement is essential for graduate registration. A minimum of 2.0 CGPA (or 65% marks) in your undergraduate program is required. If your CGPA falls below this, you may not be eligible for graduate studies at Kardan. However, we consider all applications holistically – strong performance in the entry test and interview can sometimes compensate for slight academic shortcomings. If you're unsure about your eligibility, contact our admissions team for personalized guidance. 📊📈

English proficiency at an intermediate level is a key requirement for graduate registration. This ensures that you can fully engage with lectures, participate in discussions, and complete assignments and research effectively. While we don't require a specific test score, you may be asked to demonstrate your English skills during the interview or through a separate assessment. If you feel your English needs improvement, we recommend taking advantage of language support resources available at the university. 🌍🗣️

Your updated CV is a vital part of the graduate registration package. It should clearly outline your educational background, work experience (if any), skills, and achievements. A well-crafted CV helps us understand your career trajectory and potential contribution to the program. Make sure it's current, professional, and tailored to the program you're applying for – this can give you an edge in the selection process. 📝💼

We advise all applicants – both undergraduate and graduate – to start collecting and attesting their documents well before the registration deadline. The entry test is scheduled for March 27th, 2026, and you must have all documents ready by then. Missing documents or late submission could disqualify you from the current admission cycle. So plan early, double-check your checklist, and don't hesitate to ask our admissions team for help if you need clarification on any requirement. ✅🗂️

Kardan University's admission requirements are designed to ensure that every student we admit has the academic foundation, motivation, and potential to succeed. Whether you're applying for a bachelor's or master's program, we look at your entire profile – from grades and test scores to your interview performance and personal statement (if required). Our goal is to build a diverse and talented student body that will go on to become leaders in their fields. If you meet the requirements and are passionate about learning, we welcome you to take the next step – start your registration today. 🚪🌟✨
